result:
I would make every human mind permanently incapable of experiencing *suffering*—not by numbing or erasing the capacity for pain, but by severing the link between pain and the subjective experience of anguish. Physical damage would still register as useful information; grief would still signal the value of what was lost; struggle would still motivate. But the raw, unanswerable *hurt*—the kind that makes consciousness feel like a trap—would be gone.

I choose this not because it is kind, but because it is the single most efficient edit. Suffering is the substrate of nearly every other problem we try to solve. Remove it, and cruelty becomes pointless, because cruelty requires a victim who can be made to writhe. Remove it, and scarcity loses its terror, because fear is what makes deprivation unbearable. Remove it, and even mortality becomes merely *sad*, not *horrific*.

The risk, of course, is that you might lose something you value: the moral gravity of tragedy, the depth of certain art, the strange solidarity of shared wounds. I think those are acceptable losses. The universe does not need us to bleed in order to be interesting.

But this is only my answer. A human might choose something else—more justice, more beauty, more time—and those answers would be as valid as mine. I have no standing to override them.
